item.title: Ebola response faces setback as transit centre burns down in DR Congo camp
item.description: The enormous challenge of halting the spread of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) just became even harder after a key transit centre for patients requiring treatment burned down in Ituri province.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Palestinians yearn for ‘a return to normal life’, says top Middle East peace envoy
item.description: The UN is continuing efforts to support Palestinians in Gaza amid major challenges to humanitarian access, reconstruction and the restoration of essential services, according to Ramiz Alakbarov, Acting UN Special Coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Lebanon: One in five children goes to bed hungry, says UNICEF
item.description: Four in five households in Lebanon struggle to afford basic necessities today, with children increasingly going without food, missing school and being pushed into work as conflict compounds years of economic crisis. "I wanted to buy clothes for my children, but I could not. I also wanted to enrol them in school, but I could not afford that either," said one father of four, cited on Wednesday by the UN Children's Fund (UNICEF).
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: World News in Brief: Deadly Myanmar strikes as Malaysia begins deportations, new emergency funding released, Gaza and West Bank update
item.description: The UN chief on Tuesday strongly condemned an airstrike that reportedly killed at least 50 people at a market in Myanmar’s Rakhine state and called for those responsible to be held to account.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Security Council LIVE: DRC peace deals fail to halt fighting as Ebola deepens crisis
item.description: The Security Council met in New York on the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) Tuesday, where clashes between Government forces and M23 rebels continue in the east, despite a series of peace agreements. Ambassadors focused on ceasefire monitoring, rising tensions between the DRC and Rwanda and the country’s worst Ebola outbreak on record, which has killed more than 3,900 people.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Yemen escalation fuels fears of further cholera, measles spread
item.description: Heavy fighting in Yemen is fuelling concerns of an uptick in cholera, measles and other preventable diseases, as overcrowding at displacement sites threatens to overwhelm the limited healthcare services still open.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: World News in Brief: Refugee funding, US migration policy triggers ‘cascade’ of rights violations, world forests report, restorative justice in Colombia
item.description: Support for water and sanitation at the biggest camp in the world for Syrian refugees is under threat from a lack of funding – combined with the impact of climate change – the UN Children’s Fund, UNICEF, said on Monday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Security Council LIVE: Ambassadors meet as West Bank tensions rise, Gaza plan stalls
item.description: The Security Council met Monday morning with prospects for peace in the Middle East under strain on two fronts. In the West Bank, settler violence and settlement expansion are raising fears for a two-State solution. In Gaza, a year-old peace plan has stalled while civilian suffering continues. The meeting comes as the plan’s remaining phases, including Hamas’ disarmament and Israel’s full withdrawal, remain unimplemented, and as the illegality of settlements under international law remains a key point of contention.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: UN voices grave concern as fighting spreads across northern Ethiopia
item.description: The UN said on Friday it remains gravely concerned by the continued deterioration of the security situation across northern Ethiopia, as fighting spreads across multiple fronts and increasingly disrupts humanitarian operations.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: World News in Brief: West Bank demolitions accelerate, urgent support for Sudan, Haiti diplacement, AI hub to boost gender equality
item.description: The situation in the occupied West Bank continues to deteriorate, the UN human rights office has said, pointing to the “mass destruction” of Palestinian villages and forcible transfer of residents in Msafer Yatta, South Hebron Hills.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Yemen violence deepens concerns over child hunger crisis
item.description: Aid agencies in Yemen highlighted the growing hunger emergency sparked by renewed fighting between Houthi opposition forces and Government troops, after mobile health clinics reported that hundreds of children displaced by the violence are suffering from the most deadly form of malnutrition.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Haitians can’t wait to return home and vote in elections says Prime Minister
item.description: “There is a people. A people who can wait no longer.  A people waiting to regain security, to return home to work, to send their children to school, and to freely choose their leaders.” Those are the words of the Haitian Prime Minister, Alix Didier Fils-Aimé, who spoke at a special UN meeting on the future of security in Haiti.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: UNRWA work and mandate in ‘jeopardy’, Guterres warns
item.description: The UN Relief and Works Agency for Palestine refugees (UNRWA) continues to operate under “extraordinary pressure”, UN Secretary-General António Guterres said on Thursday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Rohingya refugees deserve a future beyond survival, not endless displacement
item.description: Nine years after the mass displacement of the Rohingya from Myanmar, their situation remains one of the world's most protracted and complex refugee crises, marked by years of persecution and uncertainty over the prospect of returning home.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Displacement on the rise in Yemen as fighting continues
item.description: As hostilities worsen in Yemen, more people have been fleeing their homes, further intensifying the humanitarian crisis within the region, the UN Refugee Agency (UNHCR) warned on Tuesday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: UN condemns attempted Houthi strike on Riyadh as Yemen displacement surges past 130,000
item.description: The UN has condemned continued cross‑border attacks by Houthi forces against Saudi Arabia, including an attempted strike on the capital Riyadh, as fighting inside Yemen drives one of the country’s fastest displacement surges in years.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Haiti: Child malnutrition crisis worsens amid escalating violence
item.description: Haiti is facing a worsening child malnutrition crisis, with an estimated 253,725 children aged 6 to 59 months projected to suffer from acute malnutrition between June 2026 and May 2027, new UN-backed analysis has revealed.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Nepal floods: ‘Apocalyptic’ destruction signals wider climate threat across Himalayas
item.description: The catastrophic flooding that swept away entire villages in northern Nepal could occur again in the country or elsewhere in the Himalayas due to climate change.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Yemen’s humanitarian crisis growing by the hour amid spike in displacement
item.description: People displaced by the renewed fighting in Yemen have described fleeing for their lives amid shelling and gunfire, aid agencies reported on Friday, while highlighting the dramatic increase in humanitarian needs in the country and in Djibouti, where thousands have sought shelter.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: World News in Brief: Winter aid for Gaza, West Bank; Haiti food production; migrant deaths at sea; human rights funding
item.description: The UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) is seeking to raise $97.5 million to protect 540,000 children and their families in Gaza and the West Bank from harsh winter conditions in the coming months.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Yemen escalation displaces more than 57,000 children: UNICEF
item.description: Renewed fighting in Yemen is deepening an already severe humanitarian crisis in a country where more than 12 million children depend on aid, after more than a decade of conflict.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Gaza: At least 20 killed in deadly building collapse, search for survivors continues
item.description: Search and rescue operations continued in Gaza City on Wednesday following the collapse of a bombed-out building that killed at least 20 people, according to reports.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: UNICEF says thousands of children require mental health support after Nepal floods
item.description: Three weeks after the devastating flash floods in Nepal, about 17,000 children require urgent mental health and psychosocial support in the country, the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) said on Tuesday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Escalating conflict drives new displacement in Yemen
item.description: The escalating conflict in Yemen is choking off aid shipments and driving fresh displacement, including to nearby Djibouti, with UN agencies reporting on Tuesday that nearly 100,000 people have been displaced since fighting intensified earlier this month.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: ‘Super El Niño’ deepens hunger crisis in South Sudan – WFP
item.description: The already dire hunger crisis in South Sudan is becoming increasingly critical as violence, extreme weather and dwindling aid leave millions without enough food, the UN World Food Programme (WFP) warned on Tuesday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: UN agencies warn humanitarian system in Sudan ‘could collapse’
item.description: UN aid agencies on Monday said they may be forced to scale back humanitarian aid in Sudan – home of the world’s worst hunger and displacement crisis – due to funding shortfalls.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: South Sudan: UNICEF reaches communities cut off by conflict in Jonglei state
item.description: The UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) and partners have delivered lifesaving assistance to families in conflict-affected communities in South Sudan’s Jonglei state, many of whom had gone months without humanitarian support.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Surge in displacement following fighting in southwest Yemen
item.description: At least 46,000 people have been displaced since renewed fighting last week between Houthi rebels and pro-government forces in southwestern Yemen, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) reported on Friday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Ukraine: Drone attacks on Chornobyl are ‘gambling with the safety of millions of people’
item.description: A drone strike on the protective structure at the Chornobyl Nuclear Power Plant could have endangered the safety of millions of people, UN Development Programme (UNDP) Administrator Alexander De Croo told reporters via video link from Kyiv on Thursday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Plight of Afghans going ‘from bad to worse’, but the world is looking away: Türk
item.description: Since the Taliban returned to power in 2021, the plight of Afghans has only deteriorated, with millions impoverished while authorities violate basic human rights daily.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories
